adit_friend.about: {dock_loader} counts the captain as a friend, and keeps lists for them

clinic_scanned.about: the {cybersurgeon} read what the pod's cold took from the captain

first_friend.about: the captain found the first old friend (chapter I ends)

gabion_named.about: the battle engineer told the captain her name: {gabion}

guard_asked.about: the captain asked the impound yard's {perimeter_guard} about hulls from the needles

implant_reflex.about: the captain had a reflex implant fitted at Epsilon (a level of gunner)

medic_talked.about: the {medic} told the captain which captains send her patients

rigged_the_skirts.about: the captain helped the {battle_engineer} rig a hovertank's skirt

rode_the_trial.about: the captain rode as gunner in a live-fire trial on Delta's test range

ship_never_came_out.about: {dock_loader}'s lists show the captain's ship never came out of the needle

squad_dodged.about: the captain slipped away from the squad's sweep

the_pod.about: a needle threw the captain out; years asleep in a pod until a salvager found it; the ship did not come with them

took_vertex_array.about: the captain took the cartridge from {ancient_scholar.short}'s notes: the Vertex Array, measured in 2420 before the fire

vault_opened.about: the Kraal vault at Delta opened to the word the captain brought back from 2460

yard_list_seen.about: the captain paid the {perimeter_guard} for a look at the impound yard's list: one hull with no name

quiet: The Hansa's old hall at Alpha has a museum wing now. Its queue is shorter than the hiring hall's.
Alpha's ring traffic never stops. The controllers sleep in shifts, and so do the ships.
Beta's farm drums turn overhead, slow as a held breath. Somewhere up there a trading house is burning a surplus.
The cargo ring smells of wet soil from the drums. Even the steel here is a little green.
Lift cages rattle up from the deep levels with a shift's worth of tired faces. Nobody looks at the button for level nine.
Gamma's company store still prints its prices on paper, so nobody can say they changed overnight.
A hovertank skims the test strip past the plant, its skirt hissing on the dust. Then another. Then the first one back.
Geod's Row runs green to the horizon. The land next to it is fenced, and the fence is very well kept.
Epsilon's promenade still flies the banners of a gala nobody remembers. The holograms on them have faded to ghosts of ghosts.
The needle office at Epsilon posts its timetable in three calendars: dock time, ship time and 'other'.

Ancient Ruins Alpha.system: Tau Ceti, in the debris disk

Ancient Ruins Beta.system: Epsilon Indi, a moon of the cold giant Ab

Alien Signal Research Outpost Y.system: Sol, the outer system: a dish pointed at Lyra, past HD 178911

thirteenth_line.title: a name for the thirteenth line on level nine's plaque
thirteenth_line.about: In 2533 the plaque on level nine at Gamma has twelve names and a blank line 'for the hauler who brought the air'. In Cargo 1, after the captain helps get the miners out, {vent_boss} cuts the plaque and asks for the name. Back in 2533, the line has it, or stays blank.

vault_word.title: the word that opens the Kraal vault
vault_word.about: In 2533 {neon_sleeper} has slept too long in stasis and lost the word she chose for the family vault in 2460; the chambers take the newest memories first. In Cargo 2, newly awake at Delta, she chooses it and tells the captain. Back in 2533, the word opens the vault.

vertex_array.title: the shape of the grey alloy, measured before the fire
vertex_array.about: In 2533 {ancient_scholar}'s notes have a gap where the shape of the missing segment should be: measured from the samples, lost in the Institute fire. In Cargo 1 the captain measures the three samples at the Stellar Institute before the fire and gives her the cartridge, labelled in the captain's hand. Back in 2533 the cartridge is in her notes: the Vertex Array, which the restart will need.

intro.again.text: {origin.name} has been through 2533 once already, as {origin.rank}. The hiring hall at {place} has your face on file under another date. The clerk decides it is a filing error. In a way, it is.

intro.from_cargo2.text: {origin.name} flew the needles of 2460 as {origin.rank}. That was seventy-three years ago by the dock clocks, and a good deal less by yours. The ring you chased is a joke now. The Debacle made it one.

intro.colonel.text: {origin.name} took {serac}'s commission a hundred and thirteen years ago. The Mandate kept your rank warm. The pension office keeps it under 'missing, presumed timeless'.

intro.founder.text: {origin.name} was one of the captains who founded the Hauler Hansa. The Hansa is a hundred and thirteen years old now, and has a museum. You are in it, in a glass case marked 'presumed'.

intro.from_cargo1.text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, flew when the Hansa was new. That was a hundred and thirteen years ago by the dock clocks. Long sublight legs and longer sleeps kept you younger than the calendar. The calendar has not forgiven you.

intro.fresh.text: 2533. You have a captain's licence and a kit bag. The licence says captain. The hiring hall at {place} says able hand, and the hall is the one that is hiring.

opening.pod.title: The needle
text: Your first command went into the needle at Beta with a full hold. The needle shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for nineteen years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The needle shed you again. You know the drill by now: the file of ships, the jolt, the pod tumbling in the dark, and the long cold sleep.
The salvager who found you this time paid a finder's tenth of your own scrap value, three hundred credits, and asked if you did this on purpose. Your ship did not come with you. It never does.

The last needle you flew in 2460 shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark. As it let you go, the needle said something in needle-talk. You still remember it, and you still do not understand it.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for seventy-three years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The last needle you flew in 2460 shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for seventy-three years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The early needles were not built for haulers of your mass. One of them shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold for decades, on top of the decades your long legs had already taken. The salvager who found it was a Rockwarden prospector who knew your name from the cooperative's books. She gave you three hundred credits and would not take the pod. Your ship did not come with you.
The early needles were not built for haulers of your mass. One of them shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold for decades, on top of the decades your long legs had already taken. The salvager who found it claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.

hall.first.title: The hiring hall
text: The hiring hall at {place} is a long room with a berths board at one end and the plants' shift lists at the other. Captains post what they want and what they pay. Nobody posts what they carry.

The old hands on the benches talk about people who should be dead. A loader agrobot one hand short, older than the Hansa, still works the cargo rings. A singer rides every needle and never gets older. And a man called {serac} has not aged a day since the Debacle, or since long before it.

thought.first_work.text: No ship. The berths board pays on arrival, the plants pay by the shift, and either way I learn something.

thought.find_adit.text: The old hands say the loader agrobot works the cargo rings, Beta most of all, two turns at a dock and then on. If anything on the docks remembers my century, it does. It likes people who work the ring.

thought.the_pod.text: The world moved on while I slept in the pod. First find out who is still in it, then what became of my ship.

thought.never_came_out.text: My ship never came out of the needle. Somebody who rides the needles might know where they really go.

floor.hovertank.title: The hovertank plant
floor.hovertank.text: The plant builds hovertanks for whoever pays, the Mandate this year. The foreman says the design goes back to a legion prototype that came to Delta a century ago, flipped once, and was never quite the same.

variants.text: The first drawing in the plant's lobby is the legion's prototype, the one you delivered to Delta c a century ago. Someone has written 'mind the skirt' in the margin. The line still builds it, for the Mandate this year.
The plant's licence came through {serac}'s depot a century ago, with the prototype you sold him. The foreman calls the design 'the colonel's tank' and does not know which colonel.

floor.mine.title: The deep levels
floor.mine.text: The deep levels go down eleven now. The old hands will not go below nine, and nobody says why.

variants.text: On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth: yours. The old hands touch it for luck and will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth line you let stay blank. The old hands touch it for luck and will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth line left blank 'for the hauler'. The old hands will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
Far down the galleries a mining agrobot with a Rockwarden share badge is still boring the first gallery's fourth extension. {aela} does not stop to look. It never did. Next time, perhaps.

floor.biomass.title: The farm drums
floor.biomass.text: The farm drums turn all shift. The agrobots tend the crops, the people tend the agrobots, and nobody tends the people.

variants.text: When you clock in, the agrobots pass a pulse of light down the row. The Sowers kept the relay you let them keep, and it is a node now. Nodes remember.
Geod's Row grows from the seed stock you brought a century ago. The tender beside you says the first fields were 'given by a hauler', as if haulers gave things.

hands.plumb.title: {plumb}
hands.plumb.text: {plumb} checks her own manifest twice, then yours. 'I pay what the board says,' she says. 'The board says less than the others. That is how you know it is true.'

hands.ghillie.title: {ghillie}
hands.ghillie.text: {ghillie} named his ship the Low Water, he says, because that is when you find what people dropped. He does not say what he carries. He pays half again, and he does not ask what you carried either.

hands.caspic.title: {caspic}
hands.caspic.text: {caspic} has orders for everything, including you. 'Navigator, gunner or steward. The Mandate does not hire loaders. Loaders ask about crates.'

variants.text: {caspic} reads your file and salutes. Then he reads the date on it and stops saluting. 'Navigator, gunner or steward,' he says. 'Sir. Or not, sir. I will ask.'

hands.vrtoch.title: {vrtoch}
hands.vrtoch.text: The Errata is the last ring-research ship nobody impounded, because nobody could find its registration. 'We measure the Gyrotron's silence,' says {vrtoch}. 'It is a very precise silence.'

hands.caboose.title: {caboose}
hands.caboose.text: {caboose} blesses your kit bag 'in apparent good order and condition'. His papers say {caboose.full}, from his scan code; the old hands still call him Officer Deks, from before the Cargolytes relabelled him. The Clean Lading rides at the tail of every needle, where the Sender looks first. It is cold back there, the pay is low, and nobody asks your name.

friends.adit.title: {dock_loader}
text: The old loader agrobot works beside you for a whole shift without a word. At the end it corrects your grip. 'You will last,' it says. From {dock_loader.short}, that is a speech.
'I keep lists,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} still has the hand you brought back from Geod's Row, and the hand still says USE NO HOOKS. It knows you before you speak. 'Seventy-three years,' it says. 'I kept it oiled.'
'I keep lists now,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} turns its sensor head when you pass. 'Beta, 2460,' it says. 'You stacked badly then too.'
'I keep lists now. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
'The old manifests have your name,' says {dock_loader}. 'Your crates were always square. The loaders talked about you, the ones who trained me.'
'I keep lists. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'

choices.say: Ask about your ship
Ask who else is still alive
Work the next shift beside it

friends.adit_ship.text: {dock_loader} runs its lists, twice. 'Every hull that came out of a needle since the Debacle is in here,' it says. 'Yours went in. It never came out. Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'Ask {warp_singer}. She rides every needle. She would know where they go when they do not come back.'

variants.text: {dock_loader} runs its lists, twice. 'Every hull that came out of a needle since the Debacle is in here,' it says. 'Yours went in. It never came out. Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'You speak needle-talk. So does {warp_singer}. Ask her what the needle said to you.'

friends.adit_who.text: '{aela} still digs for the Rockwardens,' says {dock_loader}. '{neon_sleeper} sleeps at Delta between decades. {warp_singer} rides every needle and does not age. {serac} does not age either, but nobody calls him a friend. He asked about you last month.'

friends.adit_work.text: You work the next shift beside {dock_loader}. It never says a word you did not need, and by the end your grip is right. 'Now ask me something,' it says. 'Friends ask.'

sight.gamma.plaque.title: Level nine's plaque
text: Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and under them a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'.
Nobody alive knows who that was. The miners touch the blank line for luck on the way down.
Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line for the hauler who brought the air. It says {player_name}.
The letters are worn smooth where a century of miners touched them for luck. A boy in a lift cage reads your name off the plaque, then off your tag, and decides it is a coincidence.

Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, still blank. A man with a borrowed laser once asked you for a name, and you let it stay blank.
'Blank is honest,' he said. The miners touch it for luck on the way down, and wonder.

Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'. You have promised it a name.
2420 is a needle and a Gyrotron turn away. Your record carries the errand.
Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'.
That was you, in 2420. You left Gamma before the plaque was cut, and nobody wrote the name down.

choices.say: Promise the line a name (an errand to 2420)
Leave the line to the miners

errand.plaque.given.title: An errand to 2420
text: Errands to the past travel in your captain's record. To take this one to 2420, use 'captain' to export your record, then start Cargo 1 (1.3.0 or newer) as this captain.
In 2420, help get the miners out of level nine at Gamma. A few turns later the plaque is cut, and you will be asked for the name. Then start Cargo 3 again as this captain: that 2533 will remember.

thought.errand.plaque.text: Level nine's thirteenth line waits for a name. The way back to 2420 is my record: export it with 'captain', start Cargo 1 as this captain, and get the miners out of level nine at Gamma.

sight.delta.conte.title: {neon_sleeper}
text: {neon_sleeper} is awake for the restart, barely older than in 2460. She sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open.

'I chose the word myself,' she says. 'Seventy-three years in the chamber, and it went first. The chambers take the newest memories first.' The vault holds what the family kept back from the Debacle. She will share it with whoever brings the word back.
{neon_sleeper} sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open. She has lost the word; the chambers take the newest memories first.
You were in the room in 2460 when she chose it. 'Patience,' she said. 'Remember it for me, captain. I have a feeling I will ask.'
{neon_sleeper} sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open. She has lost the word; the chambers take the newest memories first.
You were in the room in 2460. The word was your idea, and she laughed at it for the first time in thirty years. She is holding it in her hand.
{neon_sleeper} sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open. She has lost the word; the chambers take the newest memories first.
'I will know it in my bones,' she said in 2460, the day she chose it. You were there. Her bones have forgotten it too. It is a Tuesday.
{neon_sleeper} sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open. She has lost the word; the chambers take the newest memories first.
You were in the room in 2460 when she chose it.
{neon_sleeper} sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open.
You have promised to bring the word back from 2460, where she is newly awake. Your record carries the errand.

choices.say: Say the word
Promise to bring the word back (an errand to 2460)
Leave her to her coffee

errand.vault.given.title: An errand to 2460
text: Errands to the past travel in your captain's record. To take this one to 2460, use 'captain' to export your record, then start Cargo 2 (2.3.0 or newer) as this captain.

In 2460, {neon_sleeper.short} still sleeps at Delta and wakes on her own schedule. Be there when she does, and be in the room when she chooses the word. Then start Cargo 3 again as this captain: in that 2533 you will know it.

thought.errand.vault.text: {neon_sleeper.short} lost the word for her vault in the chamber. The way back to 2460 is my record: export it with 'captain', start Cargo 2 as this captain, and be at Delta when she first wakes.

thought.vault_word.text: I know the word for the Kraal vault. I was there when it was chosen. {neon_sleeper.short} sits at Delta in front of a door she cannot open.

errand.vault.opened.text: The vault opens with a sigh of old air. Between deeds to land nobody has seen in a century lies a grey instrument the size of a hand: a Procrustes Analyzer. It turns two shapes until they match, whatever angle each is seen from. 'My father bought it to find ships that changed their names,' {neon_sleeper.short} says. 'Take it. You have one to find.'

sight.epsilon.notes.title: {ancient_scholar}'s notes
text: The Concord keeps a reading room at Epsilon that nobody reads in. One shelf holds {ancient_scholar}'s notes: forty years in her hand, then decades more from her upload, which writes neater than she did.
One page has a gap where the shape of the missing segment should be. 'Measured from the samples, Stellar Institute, 2420,' it says. 'Lost in the fire.'

The Concord keeps a reading room at Epsilon that nobody reads in. One shelf holds {ancient_scholar}'s notes: forty years in her hand, then decades more from her upload, which writes neater than she did.
Where the gap was, there is a square of old tape. The cartridge is in your pocket.

The Concord keeps a reading room at Epsilon that nobody reads in. One shelf holds {ancient_scholar}'s notes: forty years in her hand, then decades more from her upload, which writes neater than she did.

Where the gap should be, a data cartridge is taped to the page. The label is in your own hand: 'The shape, measured before the fire. For T.K.' Under it, in hers: 'The hauler kept their word. Whoever restarts the ring will need this.'

The Concord keeps a reading room at Epsilon that nobody reads in. One shelf holds {ancient_scholar}'s notes: forty years in her hand, then decades more from her upload, which writes neater than she did.
One page has a gap where the shape of the missing segment should be: 'Lost in the fire.' You have promised to measure the samples before they burn.

choices.say: Take the cartridge
Promise to measure the samples before the fire (an errand to 2420)
Put the notes back

errand.vertex.given.title: An errand to 2420
text: Errands to the past travel in your captain's record. To take this one to 2420, use 'captain' to export your record, then start Cargo 1 (1.3.0 or newer) as this captain.
In 2420, carry {ancient_scholar.short}'s samples to the Stellar Institute when she asks for them, and measure them there before the fire takes the store. Then start Cargo 3 again as this captain.

thought.errand.vertex.text: {ancient_scholar.short}'s notes have a gap where the shape of the grey alloy should be. The way back to 2420 is my record: carry her samples to the Stellar Institute, and measure them before the fire.

errand.vertex.taken.text: The cartridge holds the raw coordinates of the segment the builders lost: a Vertex Array. Whatever is cut to fill the ring's gap will have to be cut to this shape. Nobody else has a copy. You checked.

sight.delta.vault.title: The Kraal vault
sight.delta.vault.text: The Kraal vault stands open now. {neon_sleeper.short} keeps her coffee in it.

sight.alpha.yard.title: The impound yard
text: Behind a fence at the edge of Alpha's ring, the Mandate keeps the hulls that touched the Gyrotron before the Debacle. They wait for an audit nobody will hold.
The {perimeter_guard} walks the fence with a rifle slung the comfortable way, and does not look at you twice.

variants.text: The impound yard. The {perimeter_guard} nods to you now, the way you nod to a debt.

choices.say: Ask about hulls from the needles
Slip the guard 100 credits for a look at the yard's list
Walk on

yard.ask.text: 'Nothing in there came out of a needle,' the {perimeter_guard} says. 'Ask the docks. There is a loader one hand short that keeps lists. It knows more than the Mandate does, and the Mandate does not like that.'

variants.text: 'Nothing in there came out of a needle,' the {perimeter_guard} says. 'You know {dock_loader}? Then you know more than I do. Everyone does. I just walk the fence.'

text: Forty-one hulls, each with a registry and an audit date that came and went. And one with neither: towed in last year, tumbling, from no needle anybody logged. The paint is new. The hull under it is not.
'Not yours?' the {perimeter_guard} asks. 'Didn't think so. Nobody's is.'

Forty-one hulls, each with a registry and an audit date that came and went. And one with neither: towed in last year, tumbling, from no needle anybody logged. The paint is new. The hull under it is not.
The Procrustes Analyzer turns the nameless hull over and over and gives up: it has been cut and welded too often to match anything. Somebody did not want it found.

people.medic.title: {medic}
people.medic.text: A {medic} has a folding table at the end of the berths, a case of patches and a hand-painted sign: CASH, NO NAMES.

variants.text: The {medic} at the end of the berths looks at the way you stand and pushes a stool at you before you ask. The sign says CASH, NO NAMES.

choices.say: Get patched up (40 credits, wounds -30)
Ask who sends her patients
Leave her to her table

text: '{caboose} sends me his crews with notes pinned to their shirts,' the {medic} says. '{caspic} sends nobody, and his crews come anyway. {ghillie}'s people pay double and lie about how they got hurt.'
She does not say who pays her. She taps the sign.

sight.epsilon.clinic.title: A clinic off the research ring
sight.epsilon.clinic.text: Off Epsilon's research ring there is a clinic with one chair, and the chair has seen better centuries. The {cybersurgeon} fits implants for hands who need to be quicker than they are, and reads old damage for those who want to know.

choices.say: Have the pod's damage read (20 credits)
A reflex implant: a level of gunner (600 credits; it hurts)
Keep your head as it is

clinic.scan.text: The {cybersurgeon} reads the scan the way a pilot reads weather. 'The cold took the newest memories first. That is what cold does. The last weeks before the needle are gone, and they are not coming back. Not from me.'

text: The {cybersurgeon} reads the scan the way a pilot reads weather. 'The cold took the newest memories first. That is what cold does.'
'{neon_sleeper.short} sat in this chair last month. She wanted a word back. I told her what I am telling you: the cold keeps nothing. If you want something back, ask the past.'

clinic.implant.text: It takes an hour and a local anaesthetic that runs out halfway. Afterwards your hands move a little before you ask them to. 'Gunners love it,' the {cybersurgeon} says. 'Card players will hate you.'

sight.delta.range.title: The test range
sight.delta.range.text: Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.

variants.text: {gabion} is under the hovertank again. She waves the torch at you, which on the range counts as a greeting. The {armored_commander} raises the cold coffee.

text: Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.

'The first of these came to Delta c in a hauler's hold, a century and more ago,' the {battle_engineer} says from under the skirt. 'We still build to its drawings. The delivery note is signed, and nobody can read the name.'
Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.
'The licence came through {serac}'s depot,' the {armored_commander} says. 'Everything good comes through his depot in the end. That is what worries me.'

choices.say: Help rig the skirt (mechanic practice)
Ride as gunner in a live-fire trial (gunner: able or better)
Ask the {battle_engineer} her name
Leave them to the dust

range.rig.text: You hold the skirt panels while the {battle_engineer} welds them. She works fast and says nothing until the last seam. 'You have done this before,' she says. 'Not on a tank. On something that mattered more to you.'

range.ride.text: The {armored_commander} keeps the tank at a crawl and the targets honest. You hit four of six. 'You shoot like somebody who learned on a hauler,' the {armored_commander} says. '{serac}'s people shoot like that too. For other reasons.'

range.named.text: 'Gabion,' she says, without looking up. 'A wire cage full of rock. I build walls overnight, and the crew stopped using my rank the week I stopped a tank with one.' She holds out a hand with a burn across the palm. 'Now you know. Don't spread it around.'

squad.sweep.title: A sweep
text: A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}. Pod survivor.' A pause. 'You are on a list, hand. Not ours.' He puts the slate away. '{serac} likes to find people himself.'
A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}. Inner-systems wing, a commission nobody closed.' He looks at you properly for the first time. 'You are on {serac}'s list, not ours. He likes to find people himself.'
A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}.' A pause. 'You are on a list, hand. Not ours. {serac}'s own, in his own hand, which is never good news.'

choices.say: Show the salvager's papers
Carry the commander's kit to the next berth (loader practice)
Slip away through the cargo ring (navigator: green or better)

squad.carry.text: The kit weighs as much as you do. The {infantry_squad} relaxes a little, the way soldiers do around anyone who carries something for them. The {heavy_infantry_commander} says nothing more about lists, which is a kind of thanks.

squad.slip.text: You know the cargo ring better than the squad does. By the time the {heavy_infantry_commander} looks up again you are three berths away and somebody else's problem. He will remember the face.

people.squad.title: {infantry_squad}
people.squad.text: The {infantry_squad} is back on the berths. The {heavy_infantry_commander} nods to you, which is worse than not nodding.

variants.text: The {infantry_squad} is back on the berths. The {heavy_infantry_commander} does not nod. He writes something on the slate instead.

ch1.title: The Hiring Hall
text: 2533. The Debacle is over, and so is everything it paid for: the research houses are broke, the ring is a joke, and the hulls that touched it sit in impound yards.
Your ship is gone, and nobody can tell you where. The hiring hall opens at the start of every shift.

ch1.friend.title: An old friend
ch1.friend.text: Find someone on the docks who remembers your century.

ch2.title: Old Friends
text: Some of the people you knew are still alive, a century and more later: machines, sleepers, the ones who rode the long legs. Find them.

ch2.friends.title: Old friends found
ch2.friends.text: Find the people who outlived their century.

ch3.title: A Bridge Again
text: Someone has found you, and they have a ship and a job that nobody else will take.
